lessons.title: Basic CPU Components
lessons.concept: Computer architecture describes how hardware components are organized and interact. The CPU executes instructions and typically includes the ALU (arithmetic/logic operations), control unit (instruction coordination), and registers (small fast storage).
lessons.formula: CPU core components: ALU + Control Unit + Registers. Performance also depends on clock, cache, pipeline, etc.
lessons.worked_example: When adding two numbers, operands may be loaded into registers, the ALU performs addition, and the result is stored back to a register or memory.
mistakes: Confusing CPU with RAM or storage devices
Thinking registers are the same as main memory (registers are smaller and faster)
Assuming ALU controls instruction flow (control unit coordinates it)
lessons.provenance: Authored original lesson; not scraped. Requires independent verification before TRUSTED promotion.

lessons.title: Memory Hierarchy
lessons.concept: Memory hierarchy organizes storage by speed, cost, and capacity: registers and caches are fastest/smallest, main memory (RAM) is larger/slower, and secondary storage (SSD/HDD) is largest/slower. Faster levels reduce average access time.
lessons.formula: Typical hierarchy (fast to slow): Registers -> Cache (L1/L2/L3) -> RAM -> Secondary storage.
lessons.worked_example: Frequently used data may be kept in cache so the CPU can access it faster than fetching from RAM each time.
mistakes: Assuming all memory types have the same speed/cost
Confusing cache with RAM as separate but same-level components
Believing secondary storage is part of CPU
lessons.provenance: Authored original lesson; not scraped. Requires independent verification before TRUSTED promotion.

lessons.title: Instruction Cycle (Fetch-Decode-Execute)
lessons.concept: The CPU processes instructions through a cycle commonly described as fetch, decode, and execute (sometimes with additional stages like write-back). The control unit fetches instructions from memory, decodes them, and coordinates execution by appropriate components.
lessons.formula: Basic cycle: Fetch -> Decode -> Execute (-> Store/Write-back in many implementations).
lessons.worked_example: Fetch instruction from memory address in program counter, decode opcode to determine operation (e.g., ADD), execute using ALU/registers, then update program counter for next instruction.
mistakes: Thinking instructions are executed directly from disk without being loaded into memory
Mixing up fetch and decode responsibilities
Assuming the cycle is always a single step in modern pipelined CPUs

options.B: Reduce average time to access data/instructions from memory

practice.explanation: Cache stores frequently accessed data/instructions closer to the CPU to reduce average memory access latency compared to fetching from RAM repeatedly.
